rubrics.justification: It correctly states that no image was provided and avoids fabricating morphology, but therefore offers no actual morphological assessment.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm, endometrium, endometriosis, prior failed cycles, and transfer timing into prognosis, though some links are somewhat speculative.

The reasoning is generally logical and structured, with the low prognosis tied to endometriosis and repeated failed cycles; minor issues include speculative interpretation of Day 4 transfer and broad assumptions around RIF causes.

Much of the advice is broadly evidence-based, but recommendations such as ERA/EMMA/ALICE, NK-cell testing, immunologic therapies, and routine thrombophilia workup are not strongly supported by major guidelines for general RIF management.
It provides clear next-step suggestions for transfer review and future workup/planning, though several recommendations are more exploratory than standard-of-care.
